experiments.question: Which location earns most?
experiments.conclusion: The City earns more because of evening trade and a larger market.

experiments.question: Can the cheapest site win on low price?
experiments.change: Campus at parity vs City at a premium
experiments.conclusion: Low rent and 5-star customers cannot offset a small, price-sensitive market.

experiments.question: City or Suburb with the same best strategy?
experiments.conclusion: Location sets the ceiling; strategy decides how close you get.

experiments.question: Is a $2,000 pay lead needed?
experiments.conclusion: A $1,000 lead keeps staff at 5 stars.

experiments.question: Can training be cut to $1,000?
experiments.conclusion: No: sales fall by more than the saving.

experiments.question: Does promotion above $10,000 help?
experiments.conclusion: No: sales unchanged, so the extra spend is wasted.

experiments.question: Does roasting our own beans pay?
experiments.conclusion: Yes, through 7–8% more customers, not through cost savings.

experiments.question: Do organic beans pay?
experiments.conclusion: Yes: about twice their cost, and customers reach 5 stars at a premium.

experiments.question: Does one extra job pay for itself?
experiments.change: One extra employee kept for 5 years
experiments.conclusion: No: demand rises only in the hiring year. A people-versus-profit trade-off.

experiments.question: Roast + organic in the Suburb?
experiments.conclusion: Larger lift in the Suburb; about $24,000 of the gain is pay and training tuning.

experiments.question: Is roasting worth it in Mature markets?
experiments.change: Roasting in Mature: yes vs no
experiments.conclusion: Yes: about 20 more drinks per store per day, every year.

experiments.question: Is roasting worth it in Emerging markets?
experiments.change: Roasting in Emerging: yes vs no
experiments.conclusion: No: the small lift does not cover roaster depreciation.

experiments.question: Open Emerging own stores faster?
experiments.change: 3 more Emerging own stores a year, Years 2–4
experiments.conclusion: Yes: profit dips for two years, then overtakes.

experiments.question: Open one more Emerging store in Year 1?
experiments.change: 3 Emerging own stores in Year 1, not 2
experiments.conclusion: Yes: level by Year 3, ahead afterwards; no loss of sales per store.

rules.rule: Pick the largest market with evening demand
rules.caveat: Low rent cannot fix a small market
A discount below rivals was never tested
Customers drop to 4 stars without brand support (roasting, organic)
Higher training was not tested cleanly

rules.rule: Invest only where customers value them
rules.caveat: The Emerging penalty shrank as prices rose
Relies on keeping customers at 5 stars

rules.rule: Open early and at the maximum; stop in the final year
rules.caveat: Expect a profit dip first; yearly feedback will look bad

best.label: L3 R5 ★

notes: Game total ($) is the simulation-reported cumulative profit from Run Summary.
Target achievement count = runs where Game total >= Target.
Average game total = arithmetic mean of the 15 Game total values.
L1/L2 yearly operating profit is read from Data L1-L2.
L3 market charts use Data L3 market-year operating profit; run totals use Run Summary because Level 3 also includes all-markets/franchise results.
